detail: Speaking in Milan on Monday, Fed Governor Michael Barr said autonomous AI agents could speed up bank runs by moving deposits automatically when they spot yield gaps or stress.

items.headline: 2027 standard deduction rises to $33,200 for couples; 65+ extra goes to $2,100
items.caption: The standard deduction climbs $1,000 for married couples and $500 for singles in 2027. Older filers get a slightly bigger extra amount.
detail: Inflation adjustments lift the 2027 standard deduction to $33,200 for married couples filing jointly, $16,600 for singles and $24,950 for heads of household. These apply to returns filed in 2028.

People 65 and older get an extra amount on top: $2,100 for single or head-of-household filers and $1,700 per qualifying spouse for married filers. Blind filers get double. The separate $6,000 senior deduction still runs through 2028 and phases out above $75,000 of income for singles and $150,000 for couples.
money: Most people take the standard deduction; a higher one quietly lowers taxable income without extra work.
If your itemized deductions are close to the new amounts, 'bunching' gifts or payments into one year may help.
Seniors can stack the age-based extra with the $6,000 senior deduction if income qualifies.
risk: The $6,000 senior deduction phases out at higher incomes.

detail: US District Judge Allison Burroughs granted a preliminary injunction for Andrew Lattarulo, part owner of an immigration law firm. Agents took his phone at Boston Logan Airport in September as he returned from Aruba, copied its data and returned it eight days later. He runs a popular Instagram account with know-your-rights videos.

The judge found he would likely show the search was retaliation for protected speech, and ordered the data kept unreadable until the case ends. She did not order it destroyed or rule on the Fourth Amendment. The government denies targeting his speech and says the search was tied to an inquiry into whether his firm employed unauthorized workers.
money: Border searches of phones are legal in many cases; travelers can limit what's stored on devices they carry.
Businesses should keep work-authorization (I-9) records complete, since hiring probes can be costly.
Legal fights like this can raise costs for small law firms; budgeting for compliance helps.

The $17 billion cost would come from the state's roughly $27 billion rainy day fund, which needs legislative approval to tap. items.caption: What's new: Tyson's numbers are out. Adjusted EPS of $0.61 edged past forecasts, beef lost $1.22B for the year, and 2027 sales are guided down 3.5% to 5.5%.
detail: Tyson Foods reported fiscal fourth-quarter sales of $14.59 billion, up about 5% from a year ago and roughly $490 million above estimates. Adjusted earnings were $0.61 a share, one cent better than forecasts but down 47% from last year. Without an extra week and legal accruals, sales would have fallen 4%.

Beef remains the problem. The segment lost about $1.22 billion for the year as volumes fell and cattle costs jumped. Chicken earned about $1.75 billion and prepared foods about $1.33 billion. The company raised its yearly dividend by 2% and expects $1.7 billion to $2.15 billion in adjusted operating income in 2027. Shares rose in premarket trading.
money: A dividend payout ratio above 100% means profits don't fully cover the dividend yet; check that before buying for income.
High beef costs are hitting producers too; at the store, chicken and pork are often the cheaper protein.
Food stocks often get bought as a defensive move when tech swings; size any position with that in mind.
risk: Tyson expects lower sales in 2027, and beef could stay in the red.

items.headline: FAA outage traced to a router chain reaction; Duffy now wants $50B for air traffic control
items.caption: What's new: investigators say an Arkansas router swap set off a Texas router that flooded the network. Flights were mostly back Monday, with 284 cancellations by 7 a.m. ET.
detail: Investigators are looking at network gear at FAA sites in El Dorado, Arkansas, and Amarillo, Texas. Replacing a router in Arkansas reportedly triggered a newly replaced router in Texas to send out too much data, which overwhelmed routers at other control centers. The FAA turned off that broadcast feature on about 60 more routers.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said there is no sign of a cyberattack. He raised his request to modernize air traffic control to $50 billion, up from $30 billion. Congress approved $12.5 billion last year. Contractor L3Harris worked on the upgrades.
As of 7 a.m. ET Monday, FlightAware showed 284 canceled and 954 delayed U.S. flights. Since Friday, more than 18,500 flights were canceled.
money: If your flight was canceled, U.S. rules generally entitle you to a cash refund if you decline rebooking; ask for it.
Before Thanksgiving, book nonstop flights where you can; fewer connections means fewer chances to get stranded.
Credit cards with trip-delay coverage can repay hotel and meal costs; check your card's benefits page.
risk: The exact cause isn't confirmed, so more outages are possible during the busy holiday travel season.

items.headline: Democrats' 100-day plan: undo Medicaid cuts, extend ACA credits, restore SNAP. Who pays?
items.caption: Jeffries wants to reverse Medicaid cuts and extend ACA tax credits early next year. Proposed taxes on millionaires and buybacks would cover ACA credits, but not the Medicaid reversal.
detail: After winning the midterms, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries is calling for reversing Medicaid cuts within the first 100 days, extending Affordable Care Act tax credits and restoring SNAP funding. The CBO estimates the Republican law trims federal Medicaid spending by about $1.2 trillion through 2035, with about 13 million fewer people covered.

Making the larger ACA credits permanent would add about $350 billion to deficits over 10 years and help about 3.8 million more people get insurance, per the CBO. Other ideas include adding dental, vision and hearing to Medicare.

Proposed pay-fors include a surtax on incomes over $1 million, about $264 billion, and raising the stock buyback tax from 1% to 4%, about $242 billion to $300 billion. Critics, including the Cato Institute, doubt the plan adds up, and Trump could veto it.
money: If you buy ACA coverage, enroll by Dec. 15 at today's prices; don't count on a subsidy fix arriving in time.
On Medicaid or SNAP? Keep your income and work records current so you don't lose benefits on paperwork.
A buyback tax hike could nudge companies toward dividends; income investors may want to watch.
risk: None of this is law; a Trump veto or Senate math could block it.
Plans could change a lot before the new Congress starts.

items.headline: Social Security pays Wed. for birthdays on the 11th-20th; the 3.6% raise starts in January
items.caption: The Nov. 18 payments go to retirees born between the 11th and 20th. The 2027 COLA adds about $76 a month for the average retiree, starting with January checks.
detail: Social Security's Wednesday, Nov. 18 payment goes to retirement beneficiaries born between the 11th and 20th of the month. Those born on the 21st to 31st get paid Nov. 25. People who began benefits before May 1997, or who also get SSI, are usually paid on the 3rd.
The top 2026 monthly benefit is $5,181 for someone who claimed at 70 after maxing out taxable earnings. It is $4,152 at full retirement age and $2,969 at 62.

The 3.6% cost-of-living raise is not in these checks. It shows up in January for nearly 72 million beneficiaries and Dec. 31 for about 7.3 million SSI recipients. For the average retiree, that's about $76 more a month.
money: Don't budget the raise until January; November and December checks stay at 2026 amounts.
Check your my Social Security account for your exact 2027 amount, including any Medicare Part B change.
If a payment is late, wait three mail days before calling SSA, then contact them.
risk: Higher Medicare Part B premiums could eat into the raise for some people.

Blue J, which makes an AI tax research agent, raised $176 million at a $700 million value, partly to expand in the UK and let employees sell some shares. Traversal raised $120 million for agents that find causes of software outages, and Ocient raised $100 million for data tools.
money: AI tax tools are spreading to preparers; ask yours how they check AI answers.
Private AI deals rarely reach small investors; be wary of 'pre-IPO' share offers online.
If you work in tax, legal or finance, learning these AI tools can raise your value at work.

items.headline: IRS reminder: no itemizing needed to deduct up to $1,000 in charity gifts for 2026
items.caption: Starting with 2026 returns filed next year, standard-deduction filers can deduct cash gifts to charity. Couples get up to $2,000.

visual.title: New charity deduction
visual.foot: Permanent under the Working Families Tax Cuts law

detail: The IRS is reminding taxpayers that a permanent charity deduction for people who don't itemize begins with tax year 2026. Singles can deduct up to $1,000 of cash gifts, and married couples filing jointly up to $2,000.

Only cash gifts to qualified charities count. Donated goods, gifts to donor-advised funds and gifts to supporting organizations don't qualify. Keep receipts, bank records or a letter from the charity showing its name, the date and the amount.
money: Planning year-end giving? Gifts made by Dec. 31 count for your 2026 return.
Pay by card, check or bank transfer so you have a record; cash in a jar is hard to prove.
Couples who give $2,000 in the 22% bracket could cut their tax by about $440.
risk: Payments for raffles, galas or goods you get back may not count fully.

items.headline: Raises Jan. 1: Michigan hits $15 and Washington $17.73 as 15+ states lift minimum pay
items.caption: Workers in more than a dozen states get higher pay floors in January. Others, like Texas and Pennsylvania, stay at $7.25.
detail: Michigan's minimum wage jumps to $15 from $13.73 on Jan. 1, the biggest confirmed increase. Washington rises to $17.73, the highest statewide rate. Connecticut goes to $17.48, California to $17.40 and Rhode Island to $17.

New Jersey, Colorado, Maine, Minnesota, Ohio, South Dakota, Montana, Nebraska and Arizona also have January increases. Alaska's rise to $15 waits until July 1. Texas, North Carolina, Tennessee and Pennsylvania remain at the $7.25 federal floor.
money: Hourly workers: check your first January paycheck to make sure the new rate is applied.
A raise can change benefit eligibility; report income changes to SNAP or Medicaid on time.
Small business owners: budget now for higher payroll and any pay compression above minimum.
risk: Some employers may cut hours or raise prices to offset higher wages.

items.headline: Asia closes red before Nvidia: Kospi falls 2.8%, Nikkei 1.6%
items.caption: Chip stocks led Asia lower on Monday, a day before Nvidia reports. Hong Kong bucked the trend with a small gain.
detail: Asian markets finished mostly lower as worries about the AI trade carried into a new week. South Korea's Kospi dropped 2.8% and Japan's Nikkei lost 1.6%. Taiwan fell 4.1%.
Chipmakers took the biggest hits. SK Hynix and Kioxia each fell 5.5%, Tokyo Electron lost 5.2%, SoftBank fell 4.2% and TSMC dropped 3.4%.
Nvidia reports on Tuesday, its first report since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. Anthropic's stock debut is also set for later this week.
money: If you hold a broad Asia or emerging-markets fund, chip stocks are a big slice of it. Check how much.
Big swings before a key report can reverse fast. Avoid panic-selling a long-term fund on one day.
Hong Kong rose while others fell, a reminder that spreading money across regions can soften drops.
risk: Nvidia's results could move chip stocks sharply in either direction this week.

items.headline: Copper slides to its lowest in almost four months; BHP falls
items.caption: Copper dropped about 1.6% early Monday, and iron ore fell for a third day. Mining shares dragged Australia's market lower.

visual.title: Metals, Mon Nov 16
visual.label: LME copper hit its lowest level in almost four months.

detail: Copper fell to its lowest level in almost four months early Monday. Three-month copper on the London Metal Exchange was down about 1.6% at $13,371.50 a tonne.
Iron ore futures in Dalian fell for a third straight session. Big miner BHP lost 1.2% and copper miner Capstone fell 2.7%. Coal producer New Hope dropped 3.3% after a 10% fall in quarterly output.
Spot gold was also down about 0.2% at $3,871 an ounce.
money: Copper is often read as a gauge of global factory demand. Falling prices can hint at a slowing economy.
Mining stocks and funds tend to move with metal prices. Know your exposure before buying the dip.
Cheaper copper can eventually lower costs for wiring, electronics and home building.
risk: Metals can rebound quickly on any China stimulus or trade news.

items.headline: Australia movers: Elders jumps 7.8% on profit; Adore Beauty sinks 36%
items.caption: Farm services firm Elders posted a big profit jump. Online beauty seller Adore Beauty hit a record low after slashing its outlook.

visual.title: ASX movers, Mon Nov 16
visual.label: Adore Beauty fell to a record low of 17 cents after cutting guidance.

detail: Elders said its statutory profit rose 187% to $144 million for fiscal 2026. Underlying sales revenue climbed 31% to $4.0 billion. It held its dividend at 36 cents, and the shares rose 7.8%, the ASX 200's top gainer.
Adore Beauty fell 36% to 17 cents, a record low. It cut its fiscal 2027 underlying EBITDA guidance to $4.0 to $6.5 million, down from $9 to $13 million. Revenue for the first 20 weeks fell 8%.
Adore Beauty also said talks with its bank about loan covenants are ongoing.
money: A guidance cut can hit a small stock far harder than a big one. Size positions in small caps carefully.
Loan covenant talks are a warning sign. Check a company's debt before buying a beaten-down stock.
Strong results paired with a steady dividend often attract income investors.
risk: Prices are in Australian dollars and these are thinly traded compared with US stocks.

items.headline: IELTS co-owner IDP rejects Blackstone's third buyout offer at A$3.00 a share

IDP shares closed Friday at A$2.57, giving it a market value of about A$715 million. Blackstone's earlier offers were A$2.30 and A$2.50 a share.
In September, the board called the A$2.50 bid opportunistic and pointed to its multi-year turnaround plan.
money: Takeover targets often trade below the offer price. That gap reflects the risk the deal never happens.
Buying a stock just for a buyout is a bet. If the bidder walks away, shares can fall back.
Rejections sometimes lead to higher offers, as happened here twice.
risk: Blackstone could walk away, which could send the shares lower.

items: No evidence so far of data taken

detail: Coles, one of Australia's two big supermarket chains, is investigating a cyber incident that happened over the weekend.

money: After any store's cyber incident, watch your card statements for charges you don't recognize.
Use a unique password for each shopping account so one breach can't unlock others.
A credit freeze is free and can block new accounts opened in your name.

items.headline: Africa's MTN in early talks to buy South Africa's Telkom, four years after a failed bid
items.caption: MTN says it has expressed interest in buying all of Telkom's shares. No price has been disclosed, and the deal is not certain.

items.st: Expected to close by end of 2026

detail: MTN Group said it is in early discussions to buy all of Telkom SA's shares. It called this an expression of interest, not a formal offer.
Cash is the leading option, though Telkom holders could get MTN shares instead. Telkom is partly owned by South Africa's government. An earlier MTN bid collapsed in October 2022.
A combined company would become South Africa's largest operator by customers, ahead of Vodacom. Competition regulators would review it.
money: Early talks often end without a deal. Avoid chasing a target stock on rumors alone.
Mergers that cut competition can mean higher phone bills, which regulators try to prevent.
Emerging-market funds may hold both companies. Check your fund's top holdings.
risk: Regulators could demand spectrum sales or block the deal.

items.headline: US gas falls to $3.91 a gallon, under $4 for the first time since August

visual.title: US regular gas

detail: The national average for regular gas fell to $3.91 a gallon, according to AAA data as of Nov. 11. It's the first time below $4 since early August.
Prices fell in every state in the first week of November. North Carolina had the lowest average at $3.23. Gas is still about 92 cents higher than a year ago.
GasBuddy's Patrick De Haan said prices could stay under $4 if oil keeps falling and the Iran conflict doesn't escalate. A switch to cheaper winter gas also helps.
money: Use a gas price app before Thanksgiving trips. Prices can vary a lot within a few miles.
Store loyalty and warehouse club programs often cut cents per gallon.
Don't lock in a fuel prepay deal when prices are falling.
risk: Any flare-up in the Iran war could push prices back up fast.

items.headline: Minnesota's new ICE detention site draws protests in its first weekend
items.caption: More than 70 people rallied outside the Appleton facility, which opened Nov. 9. The government bought the former prison for $495.6 million.

visual.title: Appleton ICE facility
visual.label: Beds the former private prison in western Minnesota can hold.

detail: The Department of Homeland Security opened a detention facility in Appleton, Minnesota, on Nov. 9. The former prison can hold up to 1,600 detainees and had been empty since 2010.

CoreCivic sold the site to the federal government for $495.6 million and expects about $75 million a year under a five-year contract. DHS said the site gives ICE capacity right away without new construction.
On Saturday, more than 70 people attended a prayer vigil and rally organized by a local group. A local attorney believes more than 70 people are being held there.
money: Private prison companies earn revenue from federal detention contracts. Their stocks react to policy shifts.
Detention sites can bring jobs to small towns, but contracts can change with new policies.
Taxpayer costs for detention are set by Congress. Watch budget debates if this matters to you.
risk: Policy and funding for detention could change after the new Congress takes office.

Robotics ETFs bundle many of these firms. They can be volatile, so keep positions small.

Startup funding news hints at where big money sees growth, but you can't buy these shares directly.

items.headline: Fed officials lean toward more rate hikes; a quarter-point move expected Dec. 9
items.caption: Boston Fed chief Susan Collins says policy may need to get tighter than she thought. Vice Chair Jefferson says inflation is now the signal he watches most.

visual.title: Where the Fed stands
visual.foot: Fed minutes from October land this week

detail: Boston Fed President Susan Collins said on Friday that recent inflation data is worrying and that price pressures are spreading. She said a tighter path than she expected a couple of months ago may now be right, and later called for a steady, gradual pace of hikes.

Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said the economy is growing and hiring has stabilized, so inflation is now his main guide. Kansas City Fed President Jeffrey Schmid also said inflation is running too hot.
The Fed's benchmark rate sits at 3.75% to 4.00% after a September hike. Markets widely expect another quarter-point increase at the Dec. 8-9 meeting, and some expect one more in January.
money: Credit card and HELOC rates usually follow Fed hikes within a billing cycle or two, so paying down variable-rate debt now can save money.
High-yield savings and short-term Treasury yields tend to rise with hikes; compare your bank's rate to what's available.
If you plan to lock a mortgage or car loan soon, rate shopping before mid-December may help, since the 10-year yield is already above 5%.
risk: Fed plans can shift quickly if new inflation or jobs data surprises.
Higher rates can weigh on stock prices, especially high-growth tech.

items.headline: ULA's Vulcan rocket fails for the first time, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites
items.caption: The rocket hit trouble about 10 minutes after launch from Cape Canaveral. It is ULA's first total failure since 2006 and a setback for Amazon's satellite internet plans.

visual.title: Amazon Leo setback
visual.label: Satellites lost on Vulcan's return-to-flight launch.

detail: United Launch Alliance's Vulcan lifted off Sunday at 12:40 p.m. EST and suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into flight, failing to reach orbit. Early telemetry suggested problems around the upper stage's burn, but the cause is not yet public.
It was Vulcan's first flight in nine months and ULA's first outright rocket failure since the company formed in 2006. A long grounding is possible.
Amazon has booked 38 Vulcan launches plus flights on Blue Origin's New Glenn, Ariane 6 and SpaceX's Falcon 9. New Glenn is also still waiting to return to flight after a May pad explosion.
money: Delays to Amazon Leo could slow new competition for home internet; don't cancel a current plan expecting a cheap satellite option soon.
Launch failures can shift business toward SpaceX; investors tracking space stocks may see sentiment swing on this news.
Big setbacks like this often show up in suppliers' earnings later, so watch guidance from engine and launch partners.
risk: The cause is unknown, so the length of any grounding is uncertain.

Keep 3-6 months of expenses in cash if your industry is cutting; it buys time to find the right next job.
Laid-off workers in California can file for unemployment right away; waiting can cost weeks of benefits.

Book Thanksgiving flights early in the day; morning departures are less likely to be hit by knock-on delays.
Check whether your credit card offers trip delay coverage for hotels and meals before paying out of pocket.

items.headline: Feds sue Arkansas and Louisiana to protect Kalshi and other prediction markets
items.caption: The DOJ and CFTC say federal law, not state gambling law, governs these markets. Louisiana got a court order covering 31 firms, including Coinbase and Robinhood.

items.st: Seeks to block AG's Kalshi case

detail: The Justice Department and the CFTC sued Arkansas Attorney General Tim Griffin to stop his Nov. 4 lawsuit against Kalshi. They argue the Commodity Exchange Act gives the CFTC exclusive power over regulated event contracts.

In Louisiana, a state judge signed a temporary order requiring 31 companies, including Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase, Robinhood and Crypto.com, to stop offering event contracts to residents without a state license. The CFTC sued Louisiana the next day.
Louisiana is the 12th state the CFTC has sued. Kalshi has cut off Louisiana users, and a hearing is set for Nov. 30.
money: If you use prediction markets, your access can change overnight based on where you live; don't leave large balances parked there.
Winnings from event contracts are generally taxable; keep records for tax time.
Brokers like Robinhood and Coinbase face legal costs here; investors in those stocks may see headline risk.
risk: Courts are split, and rulings could quickly expand or shrink where these markets operate.
Treat event contracts as speculation; you can lose your whole stake.

items.headline: Apple launches a health AI study app, seeking up to 200,000 iPhone users
items.caption: Built with OpenEvidence, the app answers health questions using medical journals. Apple says data won't train AI models.

visual.title: Apple's health AI study

Answers drawn from NEJM, JAMA and Nature
Optional HealthKit sharing for tailored answers

detail: Apple and OpenEvidence released a US study app that answers everyday health questions using clinical sources such as The New England Journal of Medicine and JAMA. Users over 21 with an iPhone 15 or newer and Apple Intelligence can join.

Participants can rate answers and may share data like sleep and heart rate. Apple says data is anonymized and won't be used to train AI, and OpenEvidence deletes queries after 24 hours. OpenAI has said users ask it over 300 million health questions a week.
money: Using a free AI tool to prepare questions before a doctor visit can make a paid appointment more productive.

items.headline: About 32,000 people could lose Medicare on Feb. 1 under new immigrant eligibility rules
items.caption: Social Security sent notices Nov. 10 to enrollees whose immigration status it can't confirm. US citizens and green card holders are not affected.
detail: The Social Security Administration sent notices on Nov. 10 saying some Medicare enrollees could lose coverage Feb. 1, 2027, unless they prove their immigration status by the deadline in their letter. CMS estimates about 32,000 people are affected.

The change comes from the July 2025 tax and spending law, which removed refugees, asylum grantees, TPS holders and others from Medicare eligibility. Green card holders, Cuban-Haitian entrants and certain Pacific Island migrants remain eligible. More than 70 million people are on Medicare.
money: If you or a family member got an SSA notice, respond before the deadline in the letter; missing it can mean losing coverage.

items.headline: Pennsylvania's 'Delaware loophole' costs billions; a fix sits stalled in the Senate
items.caption: Over two-thirds of companies operating in the state pay no corporate income tax. A combined reporting bill could raise about $1.5 billion a year.
detail: Multistate companies can set up Delaware subsidiaries that collect royalties from their Pennsylvania operations. The royalties are deducted in Pennsylvania and go untaxed in Delaware. Pennsylvania is one of 18 states that still allow it, according to ITEP.

HB 1610, which would require combined reporting, passed the state House 104-99 in June 2025 but has sat in the Senate Finance Committee since September 2025. The state Chamber of Business and Industry opposes it. Meanwhile, some school districts have raised local taxes nearly 5%.
